narrative:
The model predicts a 77% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability signals that, based on patterns from many similar employees, the company sees a strong risk of you departing soon.

The decision was driven most strongly by three aspects of your profile. First, your total years of experience across all jobs had the greatest influence, pushing the prediction toward leaving. While most employees the model expects to stay have only 1-5 years of overall experience, your 6-10 years places you in a group that tends to explore new opportunities. Second, having received other job offers while at the company was the next strongest factor and also increased the likelihood of departure. Third, the time you have spent in your current role (1-5 years) further contributed to the prediction of leaving, as this tenure is typical for people beginning to look elsewhere rather than those who remain long-term.

These factors together outweighed many positive signals in your profile, such as high emotional commitment, strong job satisfaction, recognition from superiors, and useful training. Because the model sees your experience level and external opportunities as clear indicators that you may not stay, the organization has chosen not to invest in your promotion at this time.

You and your manager should discuss your career goals openly. Exploring what would make you want to remain long-term could help align expectations and potentially change this outlook. (248 words)
